clue.text: City where black groovy

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
right on is dated slang for fashionable or groovy

explanation.surface: A fragment of hip talk about a city that is cool, black and groovy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link word. Brighton is an English seaside city on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is an example of a city, on England's south coast, so a specific instance stands for the general term.

clue.text: See 19
Composer offering a bit of music to king

parts.note: a bar is a short measured unit of music
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A composer presents a short piece of music to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century, an example of the category.

clue.text: Dickensian woman, one wobbling by

parts.note: a jelly is something that wobbles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dickens character described as a woman who wobbles as she goes past.
explanation.walkthrough: JELLY here is the wobbly dessert (American jello).
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Jellyby is the philanthropist neglecting her family in Bleak House by Charles Dickens.

clue.text: Swede separated by third of carrot, say, pulled up, root around

indicators.note: the Swede's name is split open and the next piece sits between its letters

parts.note: Sven is a typical Swedish man's name, so a Swede

indicators.note: carrot has six letters, so a third of it is its opening two letters
in a down clue being pulled up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A gardener tells of turnips and carrots being uprooted while someone roots around the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' and 'carrot' suggest vegetables, but the Swede is a man's name. 'separated by' splits the name around the carrot's first third; 'pulled up' turns the example abbreviation upward, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search about for usable scraps, to rummage or root around.

clue.text: Playboy's dangling organ

definitions.meaning: a playboy is a pleasure-seeker living a dissolute life
read literally, a liver hanging free inside the body

explanation.surface: A risqué remark about a playboy's anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose liver is a dissolute person; taken literally it is also an unattached body organ.

clue.text: See 19
Our distant relative has to munch into fruit

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as eating goes into fruit

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
munch means eat

explanation.surface: Our evolutionary cousin likes to tuck into some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Great apes such as chimpanzees and gorillas are humans' closest evolutionary kin.

clue.text: Head for old money

definitions.meaning: a former British coin worth five shillings

explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the top of the head and also a pre-decimal British coin worth five shillings.

clue.text: Ex-Tory leader losing head in fit

indicators.note: the opening letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative (Tory) Party from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: A former Conservative leader is decapitated while having a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: William HAGUE is a former leader of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fit of shivering or fever, as in malaria.

clue.text: Putting on jeans, trendy to wear something woolly

indicators.note: the sheep wears the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year, a woolly creature
Levi's are a brand of jeans
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Dressing in jeans while being fashionable enough to wear a woolly jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something woolly' looks like a jumper but is a young sheep; 'to wear' puts the jeans and the trendy word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a show on means broadcasting it, so televising is putting on air.

clue.text: Small vehicle involved in accident?

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Asking whether a little car was in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something struck has been hit, as in a collision, so it was involved in an accident.

clue.text: After a beating, a grouse may be unresolved

definitions.text: After a beating, a grouse may be
definitions.meaning: on a shoot, beaters drive game birds such as grouse to take flight

explanation.walkthrough: 'beating' suggests a thrashing or a complaint ('grouse'), but it is the shoot practice of beaters flushing birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the air means still undecided; grouse flushed by beaters are literally airborne.

clue.text: Fish may be enough to feed half the biblical 5,000 in worship?

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to bless is to praise or worship

parts.words: enough to feed half the biblical 5,000
parts.note: Jesus fed five thousand with five loaves and two fishes, so one fish feeds half

explanation.surface: A biblical miracle question: would one fish feed half the crowd at worship?
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels five thousand are fed with five loaves and two fish, so a single fish suffices for half. 'in' places that number inside the worship word.
explanation.definitionFit: Filleted fish is described as boneless when the bones are removed.

clue.text: Turkish city against Scottish expression

parts.note: anti means opposed to
och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: A Turkish city set against a Scottish exclamation of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch, now called Antakya, is an ancient city in southern Turkey.

clue.text: Instrument put in through blood

indicators.note: the word in is placed somewhere, here within the next piece
running through the blood means sitting inside it

parts.note: claret is slang for blood, from its dark red colour
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: CLARET as slang for blood is common in British sports reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument, an example of the category.

clue.text: Domestic disorder in taverns

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are in disarray and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A domestic dispute breaks out in the local pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a row at home, but it is the noun for a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, someone employed to work in a home.

clue.text: What's in a vacuum? It's unimportant

definitions.meaning: a true vacuum contains no substance at all
a phrase saying something does not count or matter

explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuum' suggests a cleaner, but it is the physicist's empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: No matter means it is of no importance, and literally an absence of substance, as in a vacuum.

clue.text: Made to look ridiculous having been splatted by custard pie?

definitions.text: having been splatted by custard pie?
definitions.meaning: read literally, with a sloppy yellow filling over one's features

explanation.walkthrough: Custard pies thrown in the features are a slapstick comedy staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being embarrassed or shown up as foolish, read literally as a slapstick custard pie in the features.

clue.text: Italian food about right: I'm back for more food

indicators.note: the food goes about, or around, the next piece

parts.note: pasta is Italian food

indicators.note: the letters of the word are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner orders Italian food and promptly comes back for seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'back' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a spiced cured beef, so another kind of food after the pasta.

clue.text: A doctor with English degree, low life

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A doctor with an English degree turns out to be a lowlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low life' suggests a disreputable person, but it is the simplest form of life.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a very low form of life.

clue.text: Church with capital on plate

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A church in the capital with a collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plating, as on car bumpers, so plate here means a coating.

clue.text: Continue to haul container

parts.note: to cart something is to haul it
on as in carry on, keep going

explanation.surface: Keep on dragging a box along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a box or packet used to hold goods.

clue.text: Invitation to approach makes them heroic

indicators.note: the letters of the next words make something new when reordered

explanation.surface: An invitation turns them into heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: A come-hither look is an inviting, alluring signal to draw near.

clue.text: Nut spread

definitions.meaning: a savoury paste for spreading on toast

explanation.definitionFit: Pate is the crown of the head (slang nut); pâté is a meat paste that is spread.

clue.text: Measure of some wallop in taverns

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Measuring the amount of beer consumed in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is British slang for beer, adding to the pub picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a unit of liquid measure, eight to the gallon.

clue.text: Single life about to be lost, she stands in front of a train

definitions.text: Single life about to be lost
definitions.meaning: a woman whose unmarried days are ending

definitions.text: she stands in front of a train
definitions.meaning: a wedding dress has a train trailing behind its wearer

explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway and a suicide, but it is the trailing part of a wedding dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman getting married ends single life, and her gown's train trails behind her.

clue.text: Sensible, not 13

definitions.meaning: the opposite of the answer to 13, meaning not airborne

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is UP IN THE AIR; grounded aircraft are kept on the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounded means level-headed and also unable to fly, the reverse of being airborne.
